en: Itivuttaka 109 Catukkanipāta Brāhmaṇadhammayāgavagga Thus it was said by the Blessed One; having said this, the Well-Gone One rose from his seat and entered his dwelling. Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, a certain brahmin approached the Venerable Ānanda and, having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having exchanged greetings of friendliness and courtesy, he sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the brahmin said to the Venerable Ānanda: "Master Ānanda, what is the cause, what is the reason, why some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a place of ruin, or in hell; while others, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world? "It is because of four things, brahmin, that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a place of ruin, or in hell. What four? Here, brahmin, someone destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, and speaks falsely. These are the four things because of which some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of misery, a bad destination, a place of ruin, or in hell. But because of four other things, brahmin, some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. What four? Here, brahmin, someone abstains from destroying life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, and abstains from false speech. These are the four things because of which some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. When this was said, the brahmin said to the Venerable Ānanda: "Magnificent, Master Ānanda! Magnificent, Master Ānanda! Just as one might set upright what had been overturned, or reveal what was hidden, or show the way to one who was lost, or bring an oil lamp into the darkness so that those with eyes might see forms—it is even so how Master Ānanda has made the Dhamma clear in many ways. I go for refuge to Master Ānanda, and to the Dhamma, and to the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. May Master Ānanda accept me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forth for as long as life shall last."
The Discourse on the Stream of a River.
Thus it was said by the Blessed One; so I have heard:
"Bhikkhus, suppose a man were being carried away by the current of a river, [enticed] by what is pleasant and agreeable."
A man with keen eyesight standing on the bank, seeing him, would say:

“Good man, although you are being carried away by the current of the river because of its pleasant and agreeable appearance, there is a pool below here that is full of waves, whirlpools, and crocodiles, and inhabited by rākṣasas; you, good man, will enter that pool.”
‘Having reached it, you will either meet death or suffer pain equal to death.
Then, monks, having heard that man’s words, that man would strive against the current with his hands and feet.
Monks, I have made this simile for the purpose of making the meaning known.”
And this is the meaning herein:
“The current of a river,” monks, is a designation for craving;
“the lovely and pleasant form,” monks, is a designation for the six internal sense-bases.
“‘The lake below,’ monks, is a designation for the five lower fetters.
‘The danger of waves,’ monks, is a designation for anger and resentment.
‘The whirlpool,’ monks, is a designation for the five cords of sensual pleasure.”
“‘A house-demon,’ monks, is a designation for womenfolk.
‘Against the stream,’ monks, is a designation for renunciation.
‘Exertion with hands and feet,’ monks, is a designation for the arousal of energy.”
“‘A man with vision standing on the bank,’ monks, is a designation for the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One.
Thus the Blessed One spoke. With reference to this, it is said:
“Even with difficulty one should abandon sensual desires,
aspiring for the security from bondage in the future;
being rightly wise and well-liberated in mind,”
There, in each case, he touches liberation;
that knower of the Vedas, having lived the holy life,
is called one who has reached the end of the world and gone beyond.
This matter was also spoken by the Blessed One; thus have I heard.
The tenth [discourse].
